headline: Six days to the lockout and the starters are going fast: Griffin, Gausman and Peterson all signed Wednesday, and MLB took the union to court.

news.title: Guardians bring back Foster Griffin: three years, $48 million
news.note: Robert Murray had it first. Cleveland, the smallest payroll in baseball last spring, has now added Griffin and Kris Bubic in two days.

news.title: Kevin Gausman to the Tigers: one year, $25 million
news.note: Jeff Passan reported it, pending a physical. Gausman is the only pitcher with 30-plus starts every season since 2021.

news.title: MLB sues the players' union to protect the coming lockout
news.note: The league wants a federal judge to rule a lockout legal under antitrust law. The union called the suit 'completely frivolous.'

news.title: Luis Robert Jr. returns to the Orioles: one year, $12 million
news.note: Baltimore declined his $20 million option last month, then brought him back for less. He played three games for the O's before a hamstring strain.

news.title: Royals sign Alec Bohm: two years, $20 million
news.note: Kansas City fills third base a week after trading Maikel Garcia. The Yankees and Phillies both lose an option.

news.title: Padres closing in on a top starter; Morejon likely headed to the AL East
news.note: Kevin Acee says San Diego is close with at least one of the best starters left, with Michael King atop the list. The Padres also signed JoJo Romero for three years, $21 million.
